question.text: Secondary exits in the AIF context refer to:

answer.text: Selling AIF units or fund interests to other investors in a secondary market transaction

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (pp.216-217) defines a secondary exit of investor interest as the sale of existing unit capital or partnership interests to co-investors or outside investors at an agreed value. Because AIFs are close-ended and illiquid, such secondaries are negotiated bilaterally and require careful documentation and valuation rather than open-market trading. The Trap: A "secondary" exit is not a second round of financing into the investee, nor the fund's second investment, nor a debt refinancing. It is specifically the sale of an investor's existing interest in the AIF. Note: Source reference: NISM Series XIX-A workbook pp.216-217 (secondary sale of unit capital / partnership interest at an agreed value; close-ended, illiquid execution context).
